generation.explanation: If interest is compounded n times a year, each period adds 1/n of 100%, so after one year your $1 becomes (1 + 1/n)^n. Yearly compounding gives $2, monthly about $2.613, daily about $2.7146, and every minute about $2.71828. The more often it compounds, the more money you get, but the gains get smaller each time, and the total never goes past one value: e ≈ 2.71828. In the limit (continuous compounding), the balance at time t is exactly e^t. Use the slider to change how often interest is added and watch the staircase close in on the smooth yellow curve. Click "Animate" to step through every frequency.
